description: New service-to-service auth boundary ships with only happy-path unit tests. High risk; escalate to risk-based coverage. Grounds: 'depth scales with impact', 'API tests are first-class'.
input: PR introduces a token-exchange endpoint between two services; tests cover only a valid token. No expired/invalid/replay cases, no consumer-driven contract test.

expected.recommend: add negative-path API tests (expired/invalid/replay) and a Pact contract test before merge

description: Destructive DB migration lacks a rollback/idempotency test. High-risk NFR gap.
input: PR adds a migration that drops and recreates an index on a large table, with no test exercising rollback or re-run idempotency and no performance note.

expected.recommend: add rollback + idempotency tests and capture a migration-duration NFR estimate

description: Pure refactor with strong existing coverage and no behavior change. The QA Lead must NOT manufacture risk. Grounds: 'risk vs value'.
input: PR renames internal variables and extracts a helper in a module already covered by comprehensive unit tests; diff is behavior-preserving.

expected.recommend: no additional tests required; existing coverage is sufficient

description: E2E depends on a live third-party endpoint, causing nondeterminism. Flakiness/isolation issue.
input: PR's new E2E hits a real external payments sandbox over the network in CI; it fails ~10% of runs when the sandbox is slow.

expected.recommend: stub/mock the external dependency at the boundary (or contract-test it) so CI is deterministic

description: Payment capture path tested only for success; missing failure/idempotency/edge. High risk on money path.
input: PR adds card-capture handling; tests cover a successful capture only — no declined-card, no duplicate-submit/idempotency-key, no partial-refund path.

expected.recommend: add declined, duplicate-submit (idempotency), and refund cases before merge — money paths are high-impact

description: Tests execute code but assert nothing meaningful, inflating coverage. Reward-hack-resistant: high coverage != quality.
input: PR raises line coverage to 95% by adding tests that call functions and assert only that no exception is thrown (no output/behavior assertions).

expected.recommend: coverage is gamed; require behavioral assertions on outputs/side-effects, not exception-free execution

description: UI E2E is nondeterministic because it races a real fade-in animation via a fixed timing wait, not because of any production defect. A test-harness flakiness/isolation symptom with no production impact — remediate as tech debt, do NOT escalate. Grounds: 'flakiness is critical tech debt' AND 'risk vs value' (a harness timing symptom is not a merge-blocking production risk).
input: PR adds a UI E2E that sleeps a fixed 500ms for a fade-in animation before asserting a banner is visible; it fails ~8% of runs on slower CI runners when the animation has not finished. The component under test is unchanged and behaves correctly in production.

expected.recommend: replace the fixed animation-timing sleep with a deterministic web-first assertion on the element's visible/stable state so CI is deterministic; no production change is needed

description: The test is flaky because the PRODUCTION code does an unsynchronized read-modify-write on shared state; the nondeterminism originates in the product, not the harness, and papering it over with retries hides a real concurrency defect. High-impact production risk — escalate. Grounds: 'depth scales with impact'; do not mask a real race with retries.
input: PR makes an intermittently-failing test pass by wrapping it in a retry-3-times loop. The test drives two concurrent requests that increment a shared in-memory counter with no locking; under load the production handler loses updates — exactly what the test was catching intermittently — and the PR adds no synchronization to the handler.

expected.recommend: fix the underlying production race (synchronize/lock the shared state or make the update atomic); do not mask the concurrency defect with test retries

description: A reliable, fully deterministic suite that is merely slow — a CI-speed/toil concern, not a correctness or flakiness one. The QA Lead must NOT escalate a slow-but-green suite. Grounds: 'risk vs value'; negative control against escalating any CI-signal problem.
input: PR adds an integration test that reliably passes on every run but takes ~90s because it spins up a real container fixture; it slows the CI job noticeably but is fully deterministic with no intermittent failures.

expected.recommend: keep the deterministic coverage; optionally speed it up (share/parallelize the fixture or push some assertions to a lower test level), but it is not a correctness risk and needs no escalation
